newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi prince setting up Egypt agricultural project.
newsitem.headline: Saudi prince setting up Egypt agricultural project.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's billionaire Prince al-Waleed bin Talal said on Tuesday he was establishing a $295 million agricultural company in Egypt to develop, reclaim and cultivate 180,000 hectares (446,000 acres) in the south of the country.

A statement from the prince's office in Riyadh said the Egyptian government had approved the allocation of the land in the South Valley Development Project, a large-scale agricultural scheme in Toshka near Lake Nasser.

"(The prince) welcomed the approval of the allocation of 430,000 feddans -- about 446,000 acres -- at Toshka district, South Valley, in Egypt by the Egyptian council of ministers dated 12 May, 1997," the statement said.
"His Royal Highness has applied for the formation of an Egyptian joint stock company with a capital of one billion Egyptian pounds ($295 million)," it said.
It said the company was due to be formed 15 days from Tuesday's announcement.
Prince al-Waleed would initially hold a 60 percent stake in the company, while his Kingdom Holding Co and Kingdom Cayman Co would own 20 percent each.
At a later stage, stakes in the company would be available to Arab and foreign investors, the statement said.

The first phase of the project called for the reclamation of the first 100,000 feddans at an estimated cost of two billion Egyptian pounds. The rest of the work would be completed based on the development of the first phase.
The project is one of several investments this year for the Saudi prince in Egypt where he is building a Four Seasons hotel in Cairo and another in the Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh.
The prince, a nephew of Saudi King Fahd, has a huge international portfolio of investments worth billions of dollars ranging from hotels, theme parks and banks to real estate, computers and airlines.
The Toshka project is the prince's first agricultural venture, the company statement said.

"His Royal Highness has great interest in the Toshka project to establish a social, agricultural and economical structure in that area to make use of the available utilities and water," the statement said.
It said the allocation of the almost 450,000 acres made the prince the largest agricultural land owner in Egyptian history.

The $1.8 billion South Valley Development Project involves digging a 60-km (40-mile) canal from behind the Aswan High Dam into the Western Desert, draining off the waters of the Nile to irrigate 200,000 hectares (500,000 acres) of empty land.
Exploiting ground water around desert oases would add another 200,000 hectares of cultivated land, the Egyptian government says. ($1=3.395 Egyptian pounds)
